Fact.Name: Social Security (OASDI) wage base TY2026
Fact.Description: TY2026 OASDI contribution and benefit base = $184,500. #166: SSA, "Cost-of-Living Increase and Other Determinations for 2026", 90 FR 49047 (Nov. 3, 2025), https://www.federalregister.gov/d/2025-19763 (PDF https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2025-11-03/pdf/2025-19763.pdf), p. 49050: "The OASDI contribution and benefit base is $184,500 for remuneration paid in 2026 and self-employment income earned in tax years beginning in 2026."

Fact.Name: SE tax filing threshold
Fact.Description: Net earnings from self-employment of $400 or more generally require Schedule SE / SE tax. Cite: 26 U.S.C. § 1402; Schedule SE instructions.

Fact.Name: Primary filer: Schedule SE line 3
Fact.Description: Primary filer's Schedule C net profit or (loss) from all of their businesses, floored at $0 (no farm or optional methods). 2026 draft Schedule SE (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/f1040sse--dft.pdf, SHA-256 a59fa5dcf2f0a8a5a71c46aa3837e9e8e605eeecc0a666bcb784a368900d141c), PDF p. 2, line 2: "Net profit or (loss) from Schedule C, line 31; and Schedule K-1 (Form 1065), box 14, code A (other than farming)"; line 3: "Combine lines 1a, 1b, and 2". Line 1a is farm profit, including farm partnerships' box 14 code A. This fact is Schedule C only. Farm profit, the optional methods, church employee income, ministry or a Form 4361 or 4029 exemption, notary fees, and Form 8919 wages stop the return (/flowKnockoutScheduleSEOutOfScope) instead of being entered as zero. Box 14 code A is not added. A supported Schedule E Part II return has that box at zero. A nonzero amount stops the return (scheduleE /flowKnockoutScheduleEPartIIBox14CodeA; 26 U.S.C. 1402(a); 2026 draft Instructions for Schedule SE, PDF p. 5, Partnership Income or Loss) instead of filing line 2 without it. An unanswered K-1 question also stops the print (scheduleE /flowKnockoutScheduleEPartII). With lines 1a and 1b blank, line 3 equals line 2, so the same amount is printed on both. Each spouse files their own Schedule SE: 2026 draft Instructions for Schedule SE (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/i1040sse--dft.pdf, SHA-256 8c6b42b7d5852813bd03030c05afcd7d3126f3271a463ed007918165a0e388d3), PDF p. 3: "If both spouses have self-employment income, each must file a separate Schedule SE. Include the total profits or losses from all businesses on Form 1040 or 1040-SR. Enter the combined SE tax on Schedule 2 (Form 1040), line 4."

Fact.Name: Primary filer: net earnings from self-employment (Schedule SE line 4a)
Fact.Description: 2026 draft Schedule SE (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/f1040sse--dft.pdf, SHA-256 a59fa5dcf2f0a8a5a71c46aa3837e9e8e605eeecc0a666bcb784a368900d141c), line 4a: "If line 3 is more than zero, multiply line 3 by 92.35% (0.9235)". 26 U.S.C. 1402(a)(12) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/1402#a_12): the deduction equals net earnings times one-half of the sum of the 1401(a) and (b) rates, so 1 - (12.4% + 2.9%) / 2 = 0.9235.

Fact.Name: Primary filer: SE tax applies
Fact.Description: 2026 draft Schedule SE (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/f1040sse--dft.pdf, SHA-256 a59fa5dcf2f0a8a5a71c46aa3837e9e8e605eeecc0a666bcb784a368900d141c), line 4c: "If less than $400, stop; you don’t owe self-employment tax." 26 U.S.C. 1402(b)(2) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/1402#b_2): no self-employment income when net earnings are "less than $400". The test is per individual.

Fact.Name: Primary filer: total W-2 box 3 social security wages
Fact.Description: Sum of the primary filer's W-2 box 3 amounts, part of Schedule SE line 8a ("Total social security wages and tips (total of boxes 3 and 7 on Form(s) W-2)"). 26 U.S.C. 1402(b)(1) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/1402#b_1) reduces the base by "the amount of the wages paid to such individual", so only this filer's own W-2s count.

Fact.Name: Primary filer: total W-2 box 7 social security tips
Fact.Description: Sum of the primary filer's W-2 box 7 amounts, the rest of Schedule SE line 8a. 26 U.S.C. 1402(b)(1). Line 8b (Form 4137) and line 8c (Form 8919). Form 4137 tips stop the return (unreportedTips /flowKnockoutUnreportedTips). A yes on /hadForm8919Wages stops the return (/flowKnockoutScheduleSEOutOfScope). An answered no leaves line 8c blank, and income /wagesFrom8919 is $0.

Fact.Name: Primary filer: Schedule SE line 9
Fact.Description: 2026 draft Schedule SE (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/f1040sse--dft.pdf, SHA-256 a59fa5dcf2f0a8a5a71c46aa3837e9e8e605eeecc0a666bcb784a368900d141c), line 7 "$184,500" (/socialSecurityWageBaseTy2026) minus line 8d, not below zero: line 9 "Subtract line 8d from line 7. If zero or less, enter -0- here and on line 10". 26 U.S.C. 1402(b)(1) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/1402#b_1): self-employment income excludes the part above "(i) an amount equal to the contribution and benefit base ... minus (ii) the amount of the wages paid to such individual during such taxable years".

Fact.Name: Schedule SE line 8a: Total social security wages and tips
Fact.Description: #89. 2026 draft Schedule SE (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/f1040sse--dft.pdf, created 4/27/26), form page 1, line 8a: "Total social security wages and tips (total of boxes 3 and 7 on Form(s) W-2) and railroad retirement (tier 1) compensation." W-2 box 3 (/primaryFilerOasdiWagesTotal) plus box 7 (/primaryFilerOasdiTipsTotal) for the person with self-employment income; railroad retirement compensation is not collected. Wage-base coordination under 26 U.S.C. 1402(b)(1). Printed only; the tax itself uses /primaryFilerSeRemainingSocialSecurityWageBase.

Fact.Name: Schedule SE line 8d
Fact.Description: #89. 2026 draft Schedule SE (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/f1040sse--dft.pdf), form page 1, line 8d: "Add lines 8a, 8b, and 8c." Line 8b (Form 4137 unreported tips) stops the return (unreportedTips /flowKnockoutUnreportedTips). A yes on /hadForm8919Wages stops the return (/flowKnockoutScheduleSEOutOfScope), and an answered no leaves line 8c blank (income /wagesFrom8919 is $0), so line 8d = line 8a. Line 8a says "If $184,500 or more, skip lines 8b through 10, and go to line 11", so line 8d is $0 (printed blank) when line 8a is at least the TY2026 wage base (/socialSecurityWageBaseTy2026, $184,500; 90 FR 49047, p. 49050; 26 U.S.C. 1402(b)(1)).

Fact.Name: Primary filer: smaller of Schedule SE line 6 or line 9
Fact.Description: Base for Schedule SE line 10 ("Multiply the smaller of line 6 or line 9 by 12.4% (0.124)"); $0 when SE tax doesn't apply (line 4c).

Fact.Name: Primary filer: Schedule SE line 10
Fact.Description: 2026 draft Schedule SE (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/f1040sse--dft.pdf, SHA-256 a59fa5dcf2f0a8a5a71c46aa3837e9e8e605eeecc0a666bcb784a368900d141c), line 10: "Multiply the smaller of line 6 or line 9 by 12.4% (0.124)". 26 U.S.C. 1401(a) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/1401#a): "a tax equal to 12.4 percent of the amount of the self-employment income for such taxable year".

Fact.Name: Self-employment income: Schedule SE line 6, combined for both spouses
Fact.Description: Sum of each filer's Schedule SE line 6 (/primaryFilerSeIncome + /secondaryFilerSeIncome). Form 8959 line 13 reads it: 2026 draft Instructions for Form 8959 (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/i8959--dft.pdf, SHA-256 c5b1661eeb6cb33be840a0a01616d477d2731d2b3928e1bcd3fa13b1494bbaf1), PDF p. 5, Line 13: "Enter your self-employment income from Schedule SE (Form 1040), Part I, line 6. Combine amounts from this line if you have multiple Schedules SE." A spouse's loss is floored on that spouse's own Schedule SE, so it doesn't reduce the other spouse's self-employment income.

Fact.Name: SE tax applies to either filer
Fact.Description: True when either filer's Schedule SE line 4c is $400 or more (26 U.S.C. 1402(b)(2)).

Fact.Name: Self-employment tax (Schedule 2 line 4)
Fact.Description: Combined SE tax: each filer's Schedule SE line 12 added together. 2026 draft Instructions for Schedule SE (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/i1040sse--dft.pdf, SHA-256 8c6b42b7d5852813bd03030c05afcd7d3126f3271a463ed007918165a0e388d3), PDF p. 3: "If both spouses have self-employment income, each must file a separate Schedule SE. Include the total profits or losses from all businesses on Form 1040 or 1040-SR. Enter the combined SE tax on Schedule 2 (Form 1040), line 4."

Fact.Name: Deductible part of self-employment tax (Schedule 1 line 15)
Fact.Description: Each filer's Schedule SE line 13 added together. 26 U.S.C. 164(f)(1) gives each individual a deduction of one-half of their own 1401 taxes. 2026 draft Schedule 1 (Form 1040) line 15: "Deductible part of self-employment tax. Attach Schedule SE". Flows to /adjustmentsToIncome (taxCalculations.xml) and to Schedule 8812 line 22 through /schedule1Line15.

Fact.Name: Farm self-employment income
Fact.Description: Yes when Schedule F farm profit or Conservation Reserve Program payments belong on Schedule SE lines 1a or 1b. 26 U.S.C. 1402(a) and 1402(a)(1) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/1402#a_1): net earnings include farm income, and certain CRP payments to a person receiving Social Security or disability benefits are excluded. This tool does not compute either line.

Fact.Name: Church employee income
Fact.Description: Yes when the filer has church employee income for Schedule SE lines 5a and 5b. 26 U.S.C. 1402(a)(14) and 1402(j) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/1402#j): that income is not reduced by deductions, is not combined with other net earnings, and uses a $100 floor instead of $400.

Fact.Name: Uses a Schedule SE optional method
Fact.Description: Yes when the filer uses a farm or nonfarm optional method (Schedule SE line 4b and Part II). 26 U.S.C. 1402(a) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/1402#a), the optional-method sentences at the end of subsection (a), and 1402(l), which defines the lower and upper limits.

Fact.Name: Minister, religious order, or SE tax exemption
Fact.Description: Yes when the filer is a minister, a member of a religious order, or a Christian Science practitioner, or has an approved Form 4361 or Form 4029 exemption. 26 U.S.C. 1402(c)(4) treats that service as a trade or business. 1402(a)(8) computes net earnings without the section 107 housing exclusion. 1402(e) is the Form 4361 exemption and 1402(g) is the Form 4029 exemption (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/1402#e). Checkbox A and the housing amount are not computed here.

Fact.Name: Notary fees excluded from self-employment tax
Fact.Description: Yes when the filer has notary fees excluded from net earnings. 26 U.S.C. 1402(c)(1) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/1402#c_1): the performance of the functions of a public office is not a trade or business. The Schedule SE instructions subtract those fees from line 3 or require "Exempt—Notary." This tool does not make that subtraction.

Fact.Name: Form 8919 wages
Fact.Description: Yes when the filer has wages from Form 8919 that belong on Schedule SE line 8c. Those wages are social-security wages for the wage-base limit. income /wagesFrom8919 is $0, so a yes stops the return instead of leaving line 8c blank. Asked only when /hadSelfEmploymentIncome is yes. Form 4137 tips already stop the return (unreportedTips /flowKnockoutUnreportedTips) and are Schedule SE line 8b.

Fact.Name: Knockout: Schedule SE line this tool does not compute
Fact.Description: Stops filing and printing when a filer who had self-employment income answers yes to farm profit or Conservation Reserve Program payments (Schedule SE lines 1a and 1b; 26 U.S.C. 1402(a) and 1402(a)(1)), church employee income (lines 5a and 5b; 1402(a)(14) and 1402(j)), an optional method (line 4b and Part II; 1402(a) and 1402(l)), ministry or a Form 4361 or Form 4029 exemption (1402(a)(8), 1402(c)(4), 1402(e), 1402(g)), notary fees excluded as a public office (1402(c)(1)), or Form 8919 wages (line 8c). Complete and false when self-employment income was not asked or was answered no, and when every question is answered no. An unanswered question while self-employment income is yes stays incomplete, so those lines are not filed as zero.

Fact.Name: Schedule C section complete
Fact.Description: Interview complete for Schedule C MVP (or filer had no SE income).
